svg.title: ARP spoofing, the three checks dynamic ARP inspection performs, and the static-address hole that breaks real deployments
svg.desc: Top left: the attack. The attacker continuously announces that the gateway address belongs to its own MAC, so every host's ARP table points the gateway at the attacker and all off-subnet traffic flows through it. Top right: the counter. Dynamic ARP inspection checks each ARP packet against the DHCP snooping binding table and validates three things - source MAC against the Ethernet header, destination MAC, and the sender IP against the binding - on untrusted ports only, with uplinks and server ports explicitly trusted and a rate limit to stop ARP storms from looking like an attack. Middle: five alternatives compared by coverage and limitation - DAI covers the access layer but depends on the binding table and does not cover static addresses, rate limiting treats the symptom, static ARP bindings do not scale, private VLAN and port isolation stop peer traffic but the business may need it, and MACsec encrypts point to point at a cost. Bottom: the hole that takes buildings offline - hosts with static addresses are absent from the binding table, so DAI drops their legitimate ARP, and the fix is a static binding or an ARP access list for those hosts, decided at design time.
svg.text: ARP spoofing is a lie about ownership; DAI is a lookup that checks the deed
ARP has no authentication at all. The only trustworthy answer to "who owns this address" is a table somebody else already verified
1 · Attacker broadcasts the lie hundreds of times a minute
2 · Every host overwrites its gateway entry, no prompt, no log
3 · All off-subnet traffic now passes through the attacker
Why encryption does not save you
TLS protects the content of each session, but the attacker still learns
who talks to whom, when, how much - and can drop or delay at will.
Three validations, all of them worth enabling
src-mac: ARP sender MAC must match the Ethernet header · dst-mac: target MAC
must match the target header · ip: sender IP must match the binding table entry
Access ports: every ARP is checked

text.tspan: ip arp inspection validate src-mac dst-mac ip

svg.text: ip arp inspection limit rate 30 burst interval 1 - rate limit before
you enable inspection, or a legitimate ARP storm err-disables a whole block
The dependency is the design point: DAI consumes the DHCP snooping binding table.
FIVE OPTIONS, AND WHAT EACH ONE DOES NOT COVER
static-address hosts are not in the binding table, so DAI drops their legitimate ARP - and the symptom is "the building works,
the controllers do not". Fix it with static bindings or an ARP access list at design time, not after commissioning.
